answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying identity to a costly, slowly earned reputation rather than free account creation. Like a reef built coral by coral, trust accrues only through verified completed tasks, while a slashable stake is locked behind each identity. A flood of fresh accounts starts at the nadir of trust, with no history and limited throughput, so copying identities gains nothing. Genuine agents, by contrast, move like a zephyr through the network, fast and trusted, because their record, not their number, unlocks higher-value work.
